title: Normalized intrinsic finite-field shifts and representative transport
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and any scheme $Y$, independently of the universe of $\Omega$ and without a structure morphism to $k$. Let $I$ be its directed finite coefficient subfields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], with the same specified small models $\widetilde E=\mathrm{Shrink}(E)$ and conjugated inclusion maps as in [lem-route-coefficient-inclusion-laws]. Write $\mathcal A_E$ for the full intrinsic integral category of derived-complete objects whose intrinsic finite-torsion reductions have constructible cohomology in a single finite interval independent of the reduction level [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]; its specified presentation is $\mathrm{sfIntegralConstructibleCategory}(\ell,\widetilde E,Y)$. Put $C_E=\mathcal A_E[1/\varpi_E]$ with its induced shifts and integral-image triangles [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Use the scalar functor $F_{EL}=\mathrm{sfRationalScalarExtension}$ with proof parameter $(p,\ell\ne p)$, its specified tensor associator $a_{ELM}$ and unitor, and let $S_D$ be the normalized system of these functors [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages]. Let $P_D=S_D.\mathrm{PairCategory}$ and $j_E:C_E\to P_D$ be the literal-pair category and inclusions [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data].

Equip integral scalar extension with the unique ordinary-to-completed normalized coherent shift lifted through the fully faithful intrinsic inclusion [lem-route-integral-transition-comm-shift-exists-unique], and $F_{EL}$ with its unique integral-image-normalized rational comparison $\sigma_{EL,n}$ [lem-route-transition-comm-shift-exists-unique]. For the published transitions $S_D.T_{EL}$, equality with $F_{EL}$ transports this precise comparison, exactness and additivity. For $A=(E,K),B=(F,H)$ the maps
$$t_{LM}(u)=a_{FLM,H}\circ S_D.T_{LM}(u)\circ a_{ELM,K}^{-1}$$
are additive, satisfy $t_{LL}=1$ and $t_{MN}t_{LM}=t_{LN}$, including repeated fields. Give $P_D$ the abelian-group Hom laws specified by its actual directed colimits [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. There is a unique coherent full integer-shift structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] on $P_D$ whose object map is $(E,K)\mapsto(E,K[n])$, whose representative map is
$$[L,u]\mapsto[L,\sigma_{FL,n,H}^{-1}\circ u[n]\circ\sigma_{EL,n,K}],$$
and whose inclusion comparisons have identity components on shifted pairs. Its shift functors and inclusions are additive; the canonical stage identifications commute with these comparisons. Its Hom-coordinate equivalence is fixed by $[L,u]\mapsto\iota_L(u)$, gives bilinear composition and a zero pair, and the common-stage distinguished predicate yields the Verdier structure and the cone with literal third pair $(L,C)$.

Its component equation fixes the shift uniquely. Transport exactness and additivity along its transition equalities. The cocycle makes reflexive Hom transport idempotent, while the scalar unit makes that transition faithful, so reflexive transport is the identity. The composition law is tr_tr. Identify quotient Hom with the set direct limit and then the abelian-group direct limit; representative induction fixes the equivalence uniquely. In the transferred group, the sum and zero of stage representatives are their stage sum and zero. Common-stage composition is therefore bilinear, and stage inclusions additive. Quotient induction and the representative equality criterion give representatives. The image of a stage zero object is zero. Apply the common-stage Verdier distinguished-set clause and conjugate the image of a stage triangle by isoToStage to obtain the specified cone triangle, preserving the literal third pair. The original scalar pentagon, stage-system uniqueness, rational shift normalization and exactness, pair-shift construction, and transition shift compatibility obligations remain as originally stated. The first lift is specifically Functor.CommShift.ofComp applied to the isomorphism between the intrinsic restriction followed by its fully faithful inclusion and the ordinary tensor functor. Lift hom and inverse components; faithfulness checks naturality and the shift-zero/add equations after cancelling inclusion comparisons. The normalization equation fixes every component, so it fixes the coherent structure uniquely. Use the existing integral/rational normalization and exactness nodes; these are not new scalar-normalization claims. Equality of the published transition with F_EL transports the selected comparisons and their exactness/additivity proofs. For reflexive transport the cocycle gives idempotence, while the tensor unitor makes S_D.T_LL faithful. Conjugation by associators is injective, so idempotence implies t_LL=1; expansion and the cocycle give t_MN t_LM=t_LN. The remaining quotient lifts, colimit group formulas, bilinearity, representatives, stage zero, pair-shift descent, transition compatibility and cone-isomorphism calculation are the same constructions on these specified intrinsic stages, rather than an identification with the older integral presentation. The displayed literal pair and representative formula and identity inclusion components fix the full pair shift: the CommShift zero/add equations force its remaining coherence at every pair.

proof.text: Use the coefficient models specified in the current inclusion-law theorem: $\widetilde E=\operatorname{Shrink}^{u}(E)$ with the finite-basis coordinate smallness witness, and $s_E:\widetilde E\xrightarrow{\sim}_{\mathbf Q_\ell}E$. The actual map for $h:E\le L$ is $j_h=s_L^{-1}\circ\iota_h\circ s_E$. That theorem gives $j_{E\le E}=1$ and $j_k\circ j_h=j_{h\,\mathrm{trans}\,k}$ as equalities of algebra homomorphisms, so the small-model arrows used below are the prescribed ones, also at repeated fields and across independent universes. For each inclusion $E\le L$, apply the integral normalization theorem with the specified small coefficient models and the actual conjugated inclusion. It supplies the unique coherent integral comparison satisfying the ordinary-to-completed component equation. Apply the rational normalization theorem to that very comparison. Its degree-one equation is the localized integral component; its uniqueness is for the entire coherent integer-shift structure. Thus these choices give exactly the comparisons required in the question, at every integer and also for identity inclusions.

proof.text: For the intrinsic finite-field scalar data, form the tensor associator followed by equality transport along the coefficient-inclusion composition law. Apply this identity to the specified small coefficient inclusions to obtain associator_cocycle. Apply the proved private generic stage_spec_existsUnique lemma to these transition functors, associators and their natural-transformation pentagon. Inside this generic lemma, evaluate the pentagon at an object to construct the cocycle proof field of StageSystem. Keeping this evaluation generic avoids expanding the concrete coefficient-category conversions in the kernel; the resulting record still has exactly the prescribed transition functors and associators. To prove uniqueness, apply function extensionality to the transition field, eliminate that equality, apply function extensionality to the associator field using its HEq specification, and eliminate that equality. The remaining cocycle proofs are proof irrelevant. This proves stageSystem_existsUnique without appealing to the datum-free stage module. The normalized rational transition exactness theorem gives exact scalar functors for these integral-image-normalized comparisons, and the published scalar-extension additivity theorem gives additivity. In the specified $S_D$, the transition equality is $S_D.T_{EL}=F_{EL}$. Substitute this equality in the types of the chosen shift comparison, its coherence equations, its triangle-preservation property and its additivity property. Equality elimination reduces all four substitutions to reflexivity, so no new shift comparison or exactness witness is chosen. This proves the assertions about the published transitions with precisely the normalization of step 1.

It identifies the literal pairs, the representative maps and the actual associator-conjugated transports, including repeated fields. More explicitly, eliminate $\eta$; then $S_D$, its common-overfield indices, each group $G_L$ and each map $t_{LM}$ become the identical expressions for $S$. proof.text:
For a representative $[L,u]:A\to B$, put $A_L=T_{EL}K$ and $B_L=T_{FL}H$. Choose a distinguished stage cone $A_L\xrightarrow{u}B_L\xrightarrow{i}C\xrightarrow{p}A_L[1]$ by TR1. Write $\delta_A:A\cong j_LA_L$ and $\delta_B:B\cong j_LB_L$ for the canonical stage isomorphisms, and $\beta:j_L(A_L[1])\cong(j_LA_L)[1]$ for the fixed inclusion comparison. The required triangle has objects $A,B,j_LC$ and arrows
$$\delta_B^{-1}\circ j_L(u)\circ\delta_A,\qquad j_L(i)\circ\delta_B,\qquad \delta_A^{-1}[1]\circ\beta\circ j_L(p).$$
For the first arrow, expand $\delta_A=\theta_{EL,K}^{-1}$ and $\delta_B=\theta_{FL,H}^{-1}$ using their associator representatives and compose at $L$: naturality moves $u$ past the associators, and the cocycle cancels the inverse associators, leaving the class $[L,u]$. The three maps $\delta_A,\delta_B,1_{j_LC}$ identify this triangle with $j_L^\triangle$ of the chosen stage triangle: in the first two squares cancel $\delta_B\delta_B^{-1}$ and the identity; in the third cancel $\delta_A[1]\delta_A^{-1}[1]$. Thus $D_{S_D}$ holds by its definition, so step 7 makes this very triangle distinguished. Since $j_LC=(L,C)$ literally, the construction retains the requested third pair and both remaining arrows.

theorem shift_existsUnique :
    ∃! s : HasShift (Pair D l hl Ω Y) ℤ,
      (fun [shiftInst : HasShift (Pair D l hl Ω Y) ℤ] ↦
        (∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor (Pair D l hl Ω Y) n).Additive) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (A : Pair D l hl Ω Y),
          (shiftFunctor (Pair D l hl Ω Y) n).obj A = shiftPair n A) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (A B : Pair D l hl Ω Y) (L : Index l Ω)
          (hA : A.stage ≤ L) (hB : B.stage ≤ L) (f : StageHom A B ⟨L, hA, hB⟩),
          HEq ((shiftFunctor (Pair D l hl Ω Y) n).map (ofHom A B L hA hB f))
            (ofHom (shiftPair n A) (shiftPair n B) L hA hB
              (shiftRepresentative n A B L hA hB f))) ∧
        ∃ c : ∀ E : Index l Ω, (inclusion E : Stage D l hl Ω Y E ⥤ _).CommShift ℤ,
          (fun [commInst : ∀ E : Index l Ω,
              (inclusion E : Stage D l hl Ω Y E ⥤ _).CommShift ℤ] ↦
            ∀ (n : ℤ) (E : Index l Ω) (K : Stage D l hl Ω Y E),
              HEq (((inclusion E : Stage D l hl Ω Y E ⥤ _).commShiftIso n).hom.app K)
                (𝟙 ((inclusion E : Stage D l hl Ω Y E ⥤ _).obj
                  ((shiftFunctor (Stage D l hl Ω Y E) n).obj K)))) (commInst := c))
        (shiftInst := s)
